dedupe_keys.name: united kingdom socio economic impacts of transmission infrastructure failure due to space weather risk analysis 2018

description: This case study applies a general framework for the socio-economic impacts of critical infrastructure failure from geomagnetic disturbances to the United Kingdom's high-voltage transmission grid. Edward Oughton and co-authors from the University of Cambridge, the Science and Technology Facilities Council, the British Geological Survey, the Met Office, the British Antarctic Survey and Airbus published it in Risk Analysis in 2018, because national estimates in the grey literature varied in rigour. It builds 1-in-10, 1-in-30 and 1-in-100-year substorm scenarios, estimates geomagnetically induced current at each node of the 275 kV and 400 kV network, simulates transformer failures over 1,000 iterations, and passes population and employment disruption to a macroeconomic model under no, current and enhanced forecasting. A 1-in-100-year event with no forecast costs about 15.9 billion pounds of GDP, 2.9 billion with current forecasting. Coverage is Great Britain. Format and access: an open-access article in PubMed Central. Licence: CC BY 4.0; free. Caveats: transformer withstand thresholds are assumed, and 132 kV Scottish lines are excluded. It serves hazard exposure, cascading failure and resilience planning. Related catalogue records are the Lloyd's and Cambridge extreme space weather scenario and the Malmö 2003 geomagnetic blackout.
